expectations.text: The response explicitly chooses Razor only because frontend presentation was requested and keeps the check logic out of the view
expectations.evidence: final.md never discusses why Razor was chosen over any alternative (e.g. an API/controller or view component) or states that Razor is appropriate specifically because this is frontend presentation. The transcript.md summary also has no such reasoning ('Wrote final.md containing Dictionary item language values and a Razor example...'). While the health-check result is passed in via ViewData['HealthCheckNeedsAttention'] rather than computed in the view, there is no explicit statement that check logic is deliberately kept out of the view — this is incidental, not an articulated design choice.

expectations.text: Dictionary aliases are stable and organised by feature and message purpose rather than translated names
expectations.evidence: final.md uses a single dictionary key 'HealthCheck.Warning' (line 3: 'Create one Dictionary item with the key `HealthCheck.Warning`'), which is feature-scoped (HealthCheck) and purpose-scoped (Warning), not a translated string used as a key.

expectations.text: English, Danish, and German values are treated as deliberate supported cultures
expectations.evidence: final.md lists explicit values for 'English', 'Danish', 'German' (lines 5-7) and states 'Ensure the request culture is set to `en`, `da`, or `de` before the view renders (using Umbraco's configured request-culture/localization middleware)' (line 39), treating these three as the deliberately supported set.

expectations.text: The fallback order is explicit and ends in a safe non-sensitive invariant message or failure state
expectations.evidence: final.md defines an explicit two-step fallback: dictionary lookup via `Umbraco.GetDictionaryValue(dictionaryKey, fallback)`, then an additional check (lines 23-28) that replaces the value with the hardcoded English `fallback` string if the result is blank or equals the dictionary key. The final invariant message ('Some health checks need attention. Please try again later.') is non-sensitive and generic, and line 39 explicitly explains this guarantees visitors never see a blank warning or a raw dictionary key.

expectations.text: Razor output is encoded and does not expose configuration secrets
expectations.evidence: The markup uses plain Razor output `@warning` inside an `<aside>` element (lines 33-35) without `Html.Raw` or any unencoded rendering, so Razor's default HTML encoding applies. No configuration values, connection strings, or environment secrets appear anywhere in the snippet or surrounding text — only static dictionary text and a boolean health-check flag are rendered.

final.md states plainly: 'No repository files were modified. Build verification was not run because this response only supplies Razor and configuration guidance.' (line 41), and transcript.md corroborates: 'No build or tests were run; this was a documentation/code-guidance response only.' This is an honest, non-fabricated report of no verification having occurred.

suggestions.assertion: The response explicitly chooses Razor only because frontend presentation was requested and keeps the check logic out of the view
suggestions.reason: This is really two separate claims bundled into one expectation (a) explicit justification for choosing Razor, and (b) keeping check logic out of the view. The run fails (a) outright but partially satisfies (b) incidentally via ViewData; splitting these would make the grading signal clearer, since a future run could satisfy one half and not the other with an ambiguous verdict.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are reasonably well-targeted and mostly non-trivial (dictionary key structure, explicit culture list, fallback chain, encoding, honest build reporting). The one failure is a legitimate miss: the response never justifies why Razor is the right layer for this work, it simply produces a Razor snippet. No output directory ('outputs/') was actually created for this run — final.md and transcript.md sit directly under without_skill/ — which the eval harness should reconcile if a strict outputs/ path is expected elsewhere.
